newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Canada agree to joint car airbag research.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Canada agree to joint car airbag research.

text.p: The United States and Canada announced on Tuesday a cooperative research effort to improve the effectiveness of car airbags.
The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) said in a statement that the research would cover car crashworthiness, test dummies and new technology airbags.

Airbags are credited with saving more than 1,700 lives since first installed on some cars in 1986, but are also blamed for the deaths of 32 children and 20 women or frail adults. Many of the children were not wearing seat belts or were improperly buckled.
The NHTSA on Dec. 30 proposed that car-makers be allowed to decrease by 20-35 percent the airbag's 200 mph inflation force, a cause of many deaths.

Such a move is seen by the NHTSA as an interim step as technology is developed to build a "smart" airbag that senses when a child or small adult is in the passenger seat and automatically reduces the bag's inflation force.

The NHTSA and Transport Canada said they would work to develop systems that adjust airbag performance according to factors such as safety belt use, occupant presence, size and proximity to the airbag and the nature of the collision.
Canadian Transport Minister David Anderson said "this joint research programme will help accelerate the development of the more effective airbag of the future."
Officials noted, however, that even smart bags had to be used with seat belts, adding that seat belt use in Canada was above 90 percent and in the United States about 70 percent.
The NHTSA said that it would hold a public meeting on Feb. 11-12 to discuss the criteria for the smart airbags and procedures to test their effectiveness.
It said it expected car makers, safety advocacy groups and others to submit ideas for the new airbags.
The agency said that soon after that it would propose the industry standards for the smart bags, which it wants developed and phased in on 1999 model year cars.
